descriptor: Elevators, home lifts and mechanised car parking (BSE SME)
lede: A Kolkata maker of elevators and mechanised car-parking systems that doubled revenue in its listing year on government parking projects, and is now remaking itself as a national home-lift brand by merging Ricardo Elevators and buying a Korean parking-technology firm. Growth targets are bold (80%+ this year) but cash flow is negative and the company is small and thinly disclosed.

short_version.text: FY26 revenue doubled to ₹112 Cr with a 24% EBITDA margin and ₹17 Cr PAT; order book ₹250 Cr plus ₹70-80 Cr of Ricardo home-lift orders, which are paid largely in advance. A new plant for ₹350-400 Cr of revenue is due by March 2027, and a Korean parking-technology company (Dongyang PC, 35 countries) is being acquired.

Operating cash flow was –₹17 Cr in FY26 and negative for three years as government bills take 3-4 months; working capital ~315 days. On the May call management could not explain a ₹7 Cr goodwill impairment, results were re-uploaded with errors, and two promoter directors take ~₹2 Cr in pay on ₹17 Cr of profit.
~40x trailing earnings and ~26x EV/EBITDA; there is no listed Indian elevator peer (Otis India delisted), and SME engineering peers trade at 48-64x.

blocks.text: L.T. Elevator designs, makes and installs passenger, goods and home elevators, and through its subsidiary Park Smart builds mechanised multi-level car parking, mainly for government smart-city projects and developers in East and North-East India. In 2026 it began executing orders for Ricardo Elevators, a Hyderabad direct-to-consumer home-lift brand that sells through Meta ads and 21 experience centres, ahead of a share-swap merger.

items.text: Home lifts sell at ₹10-11 lakh with ~58-60% gross margin vs ~50% for B2B and government work.
B2C customers pay ~50% before production and 90% before dispatch; government pays on milestones, 3-4 months after billing.
Government parking projects carry higher margins and are billed mostly in H2.
Listed on BSE SME in September 2025; revenue from ₹25 Cr (FY22) to ₹112 Cr (FY26).
Ricardo merger by share swap: ~4.6 lakh new shares (~2.4% dilution).
Signed to buy 66.45% of Dongyang PC (Seoul) at US$2.85 a share, rising to 100% after a buyback; expected to add ~₹30 Cr revenue in the rest of FY27.

items.name: Base
items.text: Growth slows after FY27: ~₹250 Cr revenue at a 12% margin (₹30 Cr), valued at 28x.

items.name: Bear
items.text: Working capital and integration bite: ~₹160 Cr revenue at a 9% margin (₹14 Cr), valued at 20x.

blocks.text: Scenarios are illustrative, built on our assumptions, not company guidance.

A small company with genuine growth levers: home lifts sold digitally, government parking and a Korean technology buy. The price assumes much of that growth arrives, while cash generation and disclosure lag. Wait for H1 FY27 to show whether the 80% growth target and B2C advances are improving cash flow.
